'''Aaron Wayne Gilmore''' (born 26 August 1973) is a New Zealand former politician and member of the [[New Zealand National Party]]. He was a list MP from the [[2008 New Zealand general election|2008 election]] until the 2011 election and again from February to May 2013.

==Early years==
Gilmore was born in Christchurch to shopkeeper parents and attended Parkview Primary School, in the Christchurch suburb of [[Parklands, New Zealand|Parklands]]. He attended [[Shirley Boys' High School]], before attending the [[University of Canterbury]] where he gained a [[Master of Commerce]] degree in Economics in 1995.<ref name="Parliament bio"/>

Gilmore began his career working as an analyst with the Ministry of Transport in Wellington in 1995.<ref name="Parliament bio" /> The following year he began working at the Department of Treasury at the Crown Companies Monitoring Advisory Unit as an advisor on state owned enterprise privatisation. In 1997 Gilmore worked on secondment to SOE Minister [[Tony Ryall]], where he advised on the sale of state owned enterprises.

Gilmore left the public service in 1999 to join [[Ernst and Young]], where he worked on international projects advising utility companies. In 2001 he joined [[Cameron and Partners]] in a similar role before returning to Ernst and Young in Christchurch as a senior manager in 2004. In 2005 Gilmore worked as Corporate Development Manager at [[General Cable]], until selection as a National Party candidate.

=== First period in Parliament, 2008–2011 ===
Gilmore was selected by the National Party Christchurch East local electorate as its candidate in the safe Labour seat of [[Christchurch East]] at the end of 2007. In August 2008 the National Party announced that he would be placed at number 56 on the National Party list. Gilmore came second in the electorate race, losing to the incumbent, [[Lianne Dalziel]], by 5,765 votes, but achieved a record for National in the area of over 12,000 party and personal votes.<ref name="2008 Christchurch East final">{{cite web|title=Official Count Results – Christchurch East|url= http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2008/electorate-5.html |publisher=Chief Electoral Office, Wellington|accessdate=28 November 2011}}</ref>

Gilmore's curriculum vitae posted on the Parliament web page until 2010 listed him as a member of the [[CFA Institute|Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) Institute]], a position he never had, although he had been a provisional member. He attributed the error to the [[New Zealand Parliamentary Service|Parliamentary Service]], but a spokesman said "biographical information about MPs published on its website was supplied by them and approved by them as correct".<ref>{{cite news |title=MP's CV error made by 'somebody else' |first=Bennett |last=Adam |url= http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10679904 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=12 October 2010 |accessdate=3 May 2013}}</ref> The same online CV by Parliamentary Services contained other inaccuracies, including that Gilmore was married at the time.

In the {{NZ election link|2011}}, he again contested Christchurch East and was 53rd on the [[Party lists in the 2011 New Zealand general election#National Party|party list]]. He again placed second in the electorate behind Dalziel, and on election night results was set to be returned to parliament via the list, the last-placed candidate to be returned. However, with the counting of special votes and the release of official results, National lost a seat to the Green Party so Gilmore was not returned.<ref name="MP philosophical">{{cite news|last=Sachdeva|first=Sam|title=MP philosophical about chances|url= http://www.stuff.co.nz/the-press/news/6051525/MP-philosophical-about-chances |accessdate=28 November 2011 |work=[[The Press]] |date=29 November 2011|page=A4}}</ref>

=== Second period in Parliament, 2013 ===
In early 2013, [[Lockwood Smith]] was appointed as [[List of high commissioners of New Zealand to the United Kingdom|High Commissioner of New Zealand to the United Kingdom]] and resigned from Parliament. Gilmore was the highest person on National's party list not already in Parliament, and so he replaced Smith and became an MP again.<ref>{{cite news 
|last=Cairns 
|first=Lois 
|title=Aaron Gilmore eyes Christchurch role 
|url= http://www.stuff.co.nz/the-press/news/8111077/Aaron-Gilmore-eyes-Christchurch-role 
|accessdate=13 February 2013 |work=[[The Press]] 
|date=22 December 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news
|url= http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/8310260/Aaron-Gilmore-back-in-Parliament 
|title=Aaron Gilmore back in Parliament 
|work= Fairfax |date= 15 February 2013 |accessdate= 15 February 2013}}</ref>

Emails were released under the [[Official Information Act 1982|Official Information Act]] in May 2013 from his time as a contractor to the [[Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment]] (MBIE) in November 2012, just prior to his return to Parliament in 2013.<ref>[https://static.stuff.co.nz/files/AaronGilmoreEmails.pdf OIA emails]</ref> The emails contained comments to a Treasury Manager during an argument in which Gilmore said, after noting he may be returning to Parliament as a government member, "I am sure this sort of thing will come back to haunt you if you want your career to reach its full potential."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/HL1305/S00083/mbie-releases-aaron-gilmore-emails-text-version.htm |title=MBIE Releases Aaron Gilmore Emails – Text Version |publisher=Scoop News |date=10 May 2013 |accessdate=18 June 2014}}</ref> The emails were described as "inappropriate" by the Ministry and the Ministry. TV3 had asked Gilmore specifically, in a previously broadcast segment, whether there had been any complaints about his time at MBIE, and Gilmore had replied on camera that there was nothing that had been brought to his attention.<ref>{{cite news |author=Patrick Gower |url=http://www.3news.co.nz/Aaron-Gilmore-caught-out-again/tabid/1607/articleID/297341/Default.aspx |title=Aaron Gilmore caught out again – Story – Politics |publisher=3 News |date=10 May 2013 |accessdate=18 June 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017174927/http://www.3news.co.nz/Aaron-Gilmore-caught-out-again/tabid/1607/articleID/297341/Default.aspx |archive-date=17 October 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Departure from Parliament ===
Gilmore announced his resignation from Parliament on 12 May 2013, following a public scandal involving a restaurant in [[Hanmer Springs]], in which it is "alleged Gilmore asked the barman (who had declined to sell him more alcohol) 'Do you know who I am?' and threatened to have Prime Minister [[John Key]] intervene to have him sacked." Gilmore's resignation followed pressure from senior Ministers and the revelation that he had misled the Prime Minister.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dally |first=Andrea Vance and Joelle |date=7 May 2013 |title=Lawyer stands by allegations |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/8639144/Lawyer-stands-by-allegations |access-date=10 October 2022 |website=Stuff |language=en}}</ref> He gave his valedictory speech two days later.<ref>[http://www.3news.co.nz/Aaron-Gilmore-resigns-from-Parliament/tabid/1607/articleID/297465/Default.aspx Aaron Gilmore resigns from Parliament] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130530035932/http://www.3news.co.nz/Aaron-Gilmore-resigns-from-Parliament/tabid/1607/articleID/297465/Default.aspx |date=30 May 2013 }} ''3news.co.nz'', 12 May 2013</ref><ref>{{cite news |url= http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10883127 |title=Aaron Gilmore to resign |first=Adam |last=Bennett |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=12 May 2013}}</ref> His membership of Parliament ceased on 27 May, and his committee memberships (Maori Affairs, and Local Government and Environment) a day later.<ref name="Parliament bio">{{cite web |title=Aaron Gilmore |url= https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/former-members-of-parliament/gilmore-aaron/ |accessdate=24 November 2021}}</ref> He was replaced by [[Claudette Hauiti]].<ref>{{cite news| url=http://tvnz.co.nz/politics-news/gilmore-expected-give-his-version-events-in-final-speech-5435320|work=TVNZ |title= Gilmore expected to give his 'version of events' in final speech| date=13 May 2013}}</ref>

==After Parliament==
Gilmore runs a private property investment company, The Mighty Rocket Group, later renamed St Pauls Asset Management.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Steeman|first=Marta|date=13 March 2020|title=Former National MP Aaron Gilmore in dispute with St Pauls Apartment Body Corporate over legal fees|url= https://www.stuff.co.nz/business/property/120228206/former-national-mp-aaron-gilmore-is-in-dispute-with-the-st-pauls-apartment-body-corporate-over-legal-fees |access-date=28 February 2021|work =Stuff }}</ref> Amanda High, a former employee of The Mighty Rocket Group, took the company to the Employment Relations Authority in 2018 to enforce payment of a settlement agreed in an employment dispute.<ref>{{cite web |title=[2018] NZERA Wellington 111 3039533 |url=https://www.employment.govt.nz/assets/elawpdf/2018/c09c61bcdb/2018-NZERA-Wellington-111.pdf |website=Employment New Zealand |accessdate=2 April 2019}}</ref> Gilmore had disputed High's complaint.<ref>{{cite news |title=Former National MP Aaron Gilmore ordered to pay employee under threat of jail time |url= https://www.stuff.co.nz/business/109401567/former-national-mp-aaron-gilmore-ordered-to-pay-employee-under-threat-of-jail-time |accessdate=2 April 2019 |work=Stuff.co.nz |date=17 December 2018}}</ref>

In December 2021 Gilmore was ordered to pay NZ$11,000 in costs after a failed attempt to enforce a statutory demand against Mighty Rocket's landlord over the termination of its lease.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/business/300486642/claim-for-260000-backfires-into-bill-of-11000-for-former-national-mp-aaron-gilmore |title=Claim for $260,000 backfires into bill of $11,000 for former National MP Aaron Gilmore |author=Marty Sharpe |publisher=Stuff |date=27 December 2021 |access-date=27 December 2021}}</ref> In March 2022, he was taken to court by his parents over an unpaid loan worth more than $250,000.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sherwood |first=Sam |date=5 March 2022 |title=Disgraced former MP taken to court by his parents over $250,000 loan |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/127872463/disgraced-former-mp-taken-to-court-by-his-parents-over-250000-loan |access-date=4 March 2022 |website=Stuff |language=en}}</ref>

In July 2022 Gilmore ran for the [[Wellington City Council]] in the Eastern Ward at the [[2022 New Zealand local elections|2022 local government elections]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/dominion-post/news/wellington/129192425/disgraced-former-national-mp-aaron-gilmore-chasing-wellington-city-council-seat |title=Disgraced former National MP Aaron Gilmore chasing Wellington City Council seat |date=6 July 2022 |work=Dominion Post |publisher=Stuff |first=Bill |last=Hickman}}</ref> After announcing his candidacy, Gilmore's parents commented that he needed to "pay his bills" before he seeks a seat on [[Wellington City Council]], in reference to his unpaid debts that he owes them.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kenny |first=Jake |date=12 July 2022 |title=Aaron Gilmore 'needs to pay his bills' before running for council, parents say |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/129218356/aaron-gilmore-needs-to-pay-his-bills-before-running-for-council-parents-say |access-date=12 July 2022 |website=Stuff |language=en}}</ref> According to preliminary results, he came ninth out of ten candidates and did not win a place on the council.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 October 2022 |title=Motukairangi / Eastern Ward |url=https://wellington.govt.nz/your-council/elections/2022-elections/results/motukairangi-eastern-ward |access-date=9 October 2022 |website=Wellington City Council |language=en-NZ}}</ref>
